Heard with the aid of case diary.

This is first application filed under Section 483 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (in short "B.N.S.S."), for grant of bail to the applicant/accused, relating to FIR/Crime No.547/2024 dated (not mentioned) registered at Police Station-Jhabua, District-Jhabua (M.P.) for the commission of offence punishable under Sections 363, 366, 376(2), 376(3), 506 of the IPC and sections 5(L)/6 of the POCSO Act.
2. Prosecution story, in brief is that at the time of incident prosecutrix was minor girl aged 15 years and 10 years.

In the night of 16.5.2024 when the prosecutrix came out from her house for nature's call, present applicant and the child in conflict with law caught hold the prosecutrix and forcibly took her to Sayla, Gujarat by car.
From where present applicant returned to NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-IND:26653 2 MCRC-31381-2024 his house.
The child in conflict with law kept the prosecutrix for around 45 days alongwith him, meanwhile, he committed upon her repeatedly.
3. Learned counsel for the applicant/accused submits that the applicant has not committed the offence and he has falsely been implicated in the case.

It is submitted that main accused of the Amra @ Amarsingh vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 12 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/79246878/
1 incident is the child in conflict with law.

entities.text: Amra @ Amarsingh vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is further submitted that applicant is in custody since 06.07.2024.
Investigation is completed and charge sheet has been filed.
Conclusion of trial will take considerable long time for its disposal, therefore, it is prayed that the applicant be released on bail.
4. On the other hand, learned counsel for the non-applicant/State has opposed the prayer and submits that applicant has criminal antecedents and 7 criminal cases are pending against him.
Prosecutrix is a minor girl below 16 years of age, therefore, applicant is not entitled for grant of bail.

5. Having considered the rival submissions and after perusal of the case diary so also considering the facts and circumstances of the case coupled with the fact that prosecutrix is a minor girl below 16 years of age therefore, in view of this court, it is not a fit case to grant bail to the applicant.
Resultantly, M.Cr.C. is rejected.

(PRAKASH CHANDRA GUPTA) JUDGE ajit Amra @ Amarsingh vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 12 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/79246878/
